# Concurrent sign-key handling: theirs regenerates bob's signing key while ours
# changes bob's groups. The audit log records theirs' regen (ours did not rotate),
# and because only theirs touched .sesam/signkeys/bob.age git takes theirs' file -
# so the stored key and the log's recorded pubkey stay consistent and verify passes.

sesam-repo

exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add bob'

# OURS: change bob's groups (a log change, so the audit-log driver runs on merge).
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group-add ops
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: bob += ops'

# THEIRS: regenerate bob's signing key.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sesam user regen-sign-key --user bob
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: regen bob signkey'

exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
exec git commit --no-edit

# The regen survived, bob keeps ours' group change, and the log verifies - the
# stored signkey matches the recorded pubkey (git took theirs' single-sided edit).
exec sesam verify
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout '"operation": "user.regenerate_sign_key"'
stdout 'ops'
